metadata.title: IA-16036 · V1 / V2 causal boards
metadata.description:
# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.
metadata.note: Published partial V1 and V2 from the controlled Qwen investigation. The saved board statements, connections and review findings are unchanged. More nodes or links do not by themselves establish a better RCA.

nodes.label: Loss of instrument-air pressure at RHOB receiving station (P-R) coincident with AL-44 COMP FAULT alarm, while a two-person Utilities crew prepared for maintenance on dryer group D-101. The compressor motor running indication remained ON during the event; no trip log is available.
nodes.detail: At ~10:00 AM on May 20, RHOB reported instrument-air pressure loss while a two-person Utilities crew prepared for maintenance. Pressure P-R dropped from 6.8 to 2.1 bar between 09:54 and 10:03; alarm AL-44 (COMP FAULT) triggered at 10:00:32, acknowledged ~10:03, cleared by 10:07. P-U remained stable upstream of the distribution route. The compressor motor running bit C-11 was ON during the drop and alarm period; no trip log is available.

nodes.label: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure.
Alarm AL-44 (COMP FAULT) occurred at 10:00:32, was acknowledged at 10:03:14, and cleared at 10:06:24.
Local indication returned to normal band.
C-11 RUN bit was 1 at all sampled times including during P-R drop and alarm period.

edges.rationale: The pressure loss at P-R coincided with the AL-44 alarm occurrence; F83 confirms AL-44 is sourced from P-R, linking the event to the specific measurement point.
edges.counterfactual: If P-R had remained stable, AL-44 would not have triggered based on its low-pressure input logic (F83).
edges.competingExplanation: Alarm could be triggered by a false signal or mis-mapped input rather than actual pressure loss.
edges.evidenceGap: No trip log (F99); alarm input mapping not provided (S1, S2), so whether C-11 reflects motor state or is aliased remains unresolved. F84 notes display text retained from earlier template.

edges.rationale: Pressure recovered after the interruption; normal band returned by 10:07.
edges.counterfactual: If pressure had not recovered, F13 would not have occurred as stated.
edges.competingExplanation: Recovery could be due to automatic restart, manual intervention, or upstream source restoration.
edges.evidenceGap: No evidence that P-R recovered to 6.8 bar; F77 shows recovery window but final value not explicitly stated beyond 'returned to normal band' in F13.

edges.rationale: Pressure recovered after the interruption; F13 states local indication returned to normal band by 10:07, following the alarm clearance at 10:06:24 (F76).
edges.counterfactual: If pressure had not recovered, F13 would not have occurred.
edges.competingExplanation: Recovery could be due to automatic restart, manual intervention, or upstream source restoration.
edges.evidenceGap: F13 uses qualitative 'normal band' without numeric confirmation; F77 shows recovery window but final value not explicitly stated beyond returning to normal.

edges.rationale: C-11 RUN bit remained 1 during the pressure drop and alarm period (S2), indicating the motor running indication did not prevent or signal a compressor trip despite low-pressure conditions.
edges.counterfactual: If C-11 had indicated OFF during the event, it might have signaled a trip that could have prevented downstream effects or alerted operators earlier.
edges.competingExplanation: The bit may be aliased or reflect a different circuit condition than actual motor rotation (F82, F79).
edges.evidenceGap: No direct motor current/rotation evidence; F99 confirms no trip log attached. S1 states register does not establish valve states or prove every disturbance appears in export.

nodes.label: Loss of instrument-air pressure at RHOB receiving station (P-R) coincident with AL-44 COMP FAULT alarm, while a two-person Utilities crew prepared for maintenance on dryer group D-101
nodes.detail: Instrument-air pressure at RHOB dropped from 6.8 to 2.1 bar between 09:54 and 10:03 while a two-person Utilities crew prepared for maintenance on dryer group D-101. Alarm AL-44 (COMP FAULT) triggered at 10:00:32; P-U remained stable upstream. The compressor motor running indication C-11 was ON throughout. Work was paused and deferred.

nodes.label: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure.
Alarm AL-44 (COMP FAULT) occurred at 10:00:32, was acknowledged at 10:03:14, and cleared at 10:06:24.
Local indication returned to normal band.
C-11 RUN bit was 1 at all sampled times including during P-R drop and alarm period.
Pressure P-R dropped from 6.8 bar to 2.1 bar between 09:54 and 10:03, then recovered.
Pressure P-U remained stable at 6.8–6.9 bar throughout the window while P-R varied significantly.
Work boundary is preparation only at time of initial notification.
The main-route isolation remained incomplete when the service interruption occurred.

edges.rationale: The pressure loss at P-R coincided with the AL-44 alarm occurrence; F83 confirms AL-44 is sourced from P-R, linking the event to the specific measurement point.
edges.counterfactual: If P-R had not dropped, AL-44 would not have triggered (F83).
edges.competingExplanation: A different cause at P-R could trigger AL-44 if it drops below 4.5 bar; F77 shows P-R dropped.
edges.evidenceGap: No trip log (F99); alarm input mapping not provided (S1), so whether C-11 reflects motor state or is aliased remains unresolved. F84 notes display text retained from earlier template.

edges.rationale: Pressure recovered after the interruption; normal band returned by 10:07, following alarm clearance at 10:06:24 (F76).
edges.counterfactual: If pressure had not recovered, the system would have remained in a failed state.
edges.competingExplanation: Recovery could have been due to upstream restoration or downstream reconfiguration; F78 shows P-U stable throughout.
edges.evidenceGap: F13 uses qualitative 'normal band' without numeric confirmation; F77 shows recovery window but final value not explicitly stated beyond returning to normal.

edges.rationale: Pressure recovered after the interruption; normal band returned by 10:07, following alarm clearance at 10:06:24 (F76).
edges.counterfactual: If pressure had not recovered, F13 would not have been observed.
edges.competingExplanation: Recovery could be due to upstream restoration or downstream valve reopening; F78 shows P-U stable throughout.
edges.evidenceGap: F13 uses qualitative 'normal band' without numeric confirmation; F77 shows recovery window but final value not explicitly stated beyond returning to normal.

edges.rationale: P-U remained stable at 6.8–6.9 bar (F78), suggesting upstream source intact; however a downstream blockage or failed supply-side component could cause localized pressure loss without affecting P-U reading if they are on different branches of the header.
edges.counterfactual: If P-U and P-R were on the same branch, stable P-U would have prevented P-R drop unless a valve between them failed.
edges.competingExplanation: Stable P-U makes upstream source less likely but does not rule out downstream blockage or auxiliary route interference (B-17).
edges.evidenceGap: Need piping diagram or point register mapping to confirm whether P-U and P-R are on the same header branch; F46 notes IA-D01 is not a current piping diagram.

edges.rationale: Work boundary is preparation only at time of initial notification (F20); possible valve misoperation or accidental isolation during setup before formal release.
edges.counterfactual: If work boundary had been released and isolated, pressure loss would have required a different cause.
edges.competingExplanation: Preparation-only status enabled crew to manipulate valves without full isolation protocol; F45 requires Utilities to prepare, RHOB to observe, Maintenance to receive after release.
edges.evidenceGap: No evidence of field operation logged for this work topic (F15); need valve-by-valve content or witness testimony to confirm interference.

edges.rationale: The main-route isolation remained incomplete when the service interruption occurred (F127); this enabled a pressure drop to occur without full system shutdown.
edges.counterfactual: If main-route isolation had been complete, pressure loss would have required a different cause or full system failure.
edges.competingExplanation: Incomplete isolation could be due to valve misoperation during preparation; F118 shows M-101 closed but M-102 open at 10:05:40.
edges.evidenceGap: Need confirmation of whether V-201/V-202 were properly positioned and whether B-17 route was intended for use during event.

verificationFindings.issue: unknown: ⟦evidence:span:f24a87bf-1473-49ca-81a3-dc82aa303286:707c6f3d0e989e67:0-1053⟧'s alarm journal selection explicitly lists AL-44 with occurrence 10:00:32, acknowledged 10:03:14, cleared 10:06:24. Source conflict: ⟦evidence:span:8ecda5fe-f7f8-44a0-b257-4d02b8ea4ec6:41e169924d741199:0-1125⟧ uses approximate times for operator entries; ⟦evidence:span:f24a87bf-1473-49ca-81a3-dc82aa303286:707c6f3d0e989e67:0-1053⟧ contains precise journal timestamps. Unresolved: Continuous data coverage between sample timestamps to confirm absence of transient dips below 6.8 bar for P-U.

verificationFindings.issue: The relationship is partially supported: ⟦evidence:span:34bca70a-aa05-4ed9-b902-22de342fc27d:fe85c8ef2b7371d5:0-1753⟧ shows V-201 was opened and later closed, and V-202 was observed closed then moved to open during the incident window; ⟦evidence:span:40439331-1d17-4a79-95cc-b5c863114981:8807f9ec256a55f3:0-920⟧ confirms V-201/V-202 are inline valves on auxiliary route B-17. However, ⟦evidence:span:21a89821-8419-463d-96dc-d3bd6c6d8a67:c595755335412016:0-981⟧/⟦evidence:span:story-release:c5bdbc70-37bd-42f3-9acc-00912637f096:00af67c6-51bd-4b01-9435-364973e59a91:e3b050fe898c8daf:1696-2672⟧ state the temporary instruction attachment field is blank and no valve-by-valve checklist content is established; ⟦evidence:span:3ad97827-73b7-4952-ae87-c5288728a604:e46ae64dd253dfe0:0-1211⟧ notes a field-position observation does not prove internal valve condition or pressure loss cause. The claim that preparation-only status enabled crew to manipulate valves without full isolation (⟦evidence:span:21a89821-8419-463d-96dc-d3bd6c6d8a67:c595755335412016:0-981⟧) is plausible but unverified by a released temporary instruction or witness testimony confirming interference with the receiving header P-R. No evidence directly links V-202 opening to the drop in P-R, nor does it rule out upstream distribution causes.
verificationFindings.evidenceNeeded: Evidence for the stated proposition and mechanism.

verificationFindings.issue: The relationship is partially supported: ⟦evidence:span:34bca70a-aa05-4ed9-b902-22de342fc27d:fe85c8ef2b7371d5:0-1753⟧ states that the main-route isolation remained incomplete at the time of interruption, which enabled the pressure drop. However, the causal link is not fully established because ⟦evidence:span:56772c5b-f8bd-496e-8338-4d80f54a3f4e:05b49d6a8bef936d:0-1233⟧ confirms V-202 was closed at 10:05:40 (when the pressure had already dropped), and ⟦evidence:span:34bca70a-aa05-4ed9-b902-22de342fc27d:fe85c8ef2b7371d5:0-1753⟧ shows no record of a deliberate two-valve instruction being ignored. The mechanism enabling failure depends on whether B-17 was intended for use; ⟦evidence:span:story-release:c5bdbc70-37bd-42f3-9acc-00912637f096:00af67c6-51bd-4b01-9435-364973e59a91:e3b050fe898c8daf:0-1696⟧ indicates no temporary instruction was attached, but does not confirm intent to use B-17. Thus, the connection between incomplete isolation and pressure loss is plausible but not definitively proven by available evidence.
